name: ssh-audit
what: A Python tool that connects to SSH servers (or acts as a server to test SSH clients) and reports the banner, software version, key-exchange, host-key, cipher and MAC algorithms with fail/warn/info ratings. It also checks configurations against built-in or custom policies and can print platform hardening guides. It does not test authentication, so it cannot confirm or exploit auth bypasses such as CVE-2026-123158; use it to find and baseline sshd fleets.
when: When you need a quick inventory of which SSH daemons are listening and what they announce (for example, to find OpenSSH builds on Alpine after an advisory), and as a recurring policy check on jump hosts, Linux servers and network appliances you own or are authorised to assess.
example: Install from PyPI with `pip3 install ssh-audit` (release 3.9.0 was current when checked on 9 November 2026), or use the Docker image `positronsecurity/ssh-audit`.
Audit one host without the connection-rate test: `ssh-audit --skip-rate-test bastion01.example.internal`. Exit code 0 means every algorithm is rated secure.

Audit a list of in-scope hosts (`HOST[:PORT]` per line) and keep machine-readable output: `ssh-audit --skip-rate-test -T in-scope-ssh.txt -jj > ssh-audit.json`, then filter the JSON for the banner and software fields.

Baseline a known-good server as a custom policy with `ssh-audit -M hardened_policy.txt gold-host`, then check the fleet against it with `ssh-audit -P hardened_policy.txt -T in-scope-ssh.txt`. List built-in policies with `ssh-audit -L`.

Print a vendor-neutral hardening config for a platform with `ssh-audit --list-hardening-guides` and `ssh-audit --get-hardening-guide "<platform name>"`, and review it before applying through change control.
pitfalls: A standard audit runs a connection-rate test (to infer DHEat exposure) unless you pass `--skip-rate-test`; on fragile appliances or rate-limited jump hosts, skip it.
`--dheat` actively runs the DHEat denial-of-service attack (CVE-2002-20001) against the target. Never run it outside an agreed test window with written authorisation.

The banner shows the upstream version (for example OpenSSH_10.0), not the distribution patch level. A backported fix such as Alpine 3.22's 10.0_p1-r11 still announces 10.0 — confirm the package version on the host.
It audits algorithms and policy, not authentication settings like PasswordAuthentication or UsePAM; check those with `sshd -T` on the host.
Only test systems you own or have written permission to test.
